name: Benin
headline: Benin: +8.1% growth in 2025, 1.1% inflation, debt 59% of GDP
sections: Benin is a $24.6 billion economy (2025), the world's 126th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +8.1% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $4,817 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 10.2% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 1.1% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges. Unemployment stood at 1.6% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 2.9% (2025).
Gross government debt is 59% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has risen from 46% in 2020. The general government balance is −2.7% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is −5.7% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 37% of GDP (2025), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 2.0% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 50% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 61.0 years (2024). Population: 14.8 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
